claims.text: Views At least 2 views taken in different planes, usually AP and lateral
claims.quote: They should include at least 2 views taken in different planes (usually anteroposterior and lateral views).

claims.text: Examine the joint above and below the injury, because concomitant injuries and referred pain are common
claims.quote: The joint above and below the injury should also be examined, because concomitant injuries and referred pain are common.

claims.text: Bone Fractures: white bone shows up well against the gray soft tissue next to it
claims.quote: Fractures: White bone is well seen because it is adjacent to gray soft tissues.

claims.text: A greenstick fracture shows as a discontinuity (step-off) in the cortex
claims.quote: This radiograph shows a greenstick fracture of the distal radius, visible as a discontinuity (step-off) in the radial aspect of the cortex (arrow).

claims.text: Lesions: lytic or blastic; prostate cancer metastases are most often blastic, lung cancer most often lytic, breast cancer either
claims.quote: Prostate cancer is most often blastic, lung cancer is most often lytic, and breast cancer may be blastic or lytic.

claims.text: Periosteum: osteomyelitis shows periosteal elevation, bone destruction and soft-tissue swelling, but only after 2 to 4 weeks
claims.quote: Radiographs become abnormal after 2 to 4 weeks, showing periosteal elevation, bone destruction, soft-tissue swelling

claims.text: Joints Osteoarthritis: marginal osteophytes, joint space narrowing, denser subchondral bone, subchondral cysts and bony remodeling
claims.quote: Radiographs generally reveal marginal osteophytes, narrowing of the joint space, increased density of the subchondral bone, subchondral cyst formation, bony remodeling, and sometimes joint effusions.

claims.text: Rheumatoid arthritis: soft-tissue swelling first; later periarticular osteoporosis, joint space narrowing and marginal erosions
claims.quote: Radiographs show only soft-tissue swelling during the first months of disease. Subsequently, periarticular osteoporosis, joint space (articular cartilage) narrowing, and marginal erosions may become visible.

claims.text: Soft tissue Radiographs show mainly bone, plus joint effusion from bleeding or an occult fracture
claims.quote: Radiographs show primarily bone (and joint effusion secondary to bleeding or occult fracture) and thus are useful for diagnosing fractures.

claims.text: If the film is normal but suspicion is high A fracture line that is not visible at first can usually be seen about 1 week after the injury
claims.quote: If a fracture line is not initially visible on radiograph (eg, in some nondisplaced fractures), it typically can be detected about 1 week after the injury

claims.text: Consider MRI (sometimes CT) when radiographs are normal but a fracture is strongly suspected, such as an older adult who cannot walk after a fall
claims.quote: Consider MRI (sometimes CT) when radiographs are normal but a fracture is strongly suspected clinically (eg, in an older adult who has hip pain and cannot walk after a fall and initial radiographs are normal).
